subject: Medford High School ADA Compliance and Infrastructure
overview: The commission met to discuss infrastructure accessibility issues across the city, including sidewalk projects and school parking lot compliance. Key outcomes included the approval of past minutes, the procurement of updated ADA signage, and the rescheduling of the next meeting.

items.title: Introductions and Secretary Recruitment
items.summary: Commissioners and guests introduced themselves, and Gabrielle Evangelista volunteered to assist with note-taking in the absence of a permanent secretary.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the September meeting minutes as amended to reflect a unanimous vote outcome.

items.title: Commission Vacancies and Membership Process
items.summary: The commission reviewed the status of four prospective candidates for three vacancies and discussed the bylaw requirement for a majority representation of persons with disabilities.

items.title: Harvest Your Energy Festival Recap
items.summary: Members discussed outreach efforts at the festival and identified the need for branded materials like table skirts, banners, and reusable trifold displays.

items.title: Infrastructure and Sidewalk Accessibility
items.summary: Concerns were raised regarding non-navigable sidewalk paving on Fellsway West and the lack of curb cuts near major commercial intersections. The liaison committed to touring the sites with city engineers to address ADA compliance.

items.title: Medford High School ADA Priorities
items.summary: Susan Bibbins reported that new speed bumps at the high school are obstructing accessible parking and curb cuts. The liaison announced that ARPA-funded signage with modern accessibility icons is being ordered for city buildings.

items.title: Digital Accessibility and Website Updates
items.summary: Linda Smith offered to assist with improving the digital accessibility of the commission's webpage and removing outdated contact information.

items.title: Grants and Outreach Goals
items.summary: The commission discussed pursuing a $12,000 grant from the Mass Office of Public Health for structural improvements and setting focused goals for the upcoming year.

items.title: Correspondence, Announcements, and Voting Link
items.summary: Announcements included upcoming disability summits and accessibility monitoring training; the liaison also coordinated adding an accessible voting link to the city website.

items.title: Public Participation and Meeting Schedule
items.summary: Yvette Evangelista suggested using hands-free audio capture for public events. The commission voted to reschedule the November meeting to November 30th to avoid the Thanksgiving holiday.
